newsitem.title: USA: Tampa, Fla., okays aquarium bond refinancing.
newsitem.headline: Tampa, Fla., okays aquarium bond refinancing.

text.p: Tampa City Council gave final approval Thursday to a plan to aquire the struggling Florida Aquarium and refinance its bonds, city chief accountant Ron Ibarra said.
The plan calls for the city to defease the aquarium's outstanding bonds and issue $84 million of City of Tampa revenue bonds for the facility, tentatively by Nov 1.
"It's going to be a tight squeeze," Ibarra said.
Merrill Lynch & Co is senior manager on the deal with Raymond James & Associates Inc, Smith Barney Inc and Douglas James Securities Inc as co-managers.

Attendance at the two-year-old aquarium has fallen well below projections and the facility was forced to dip into reserves to make its $3.2 million debt service payment in May. It would have had to do so again to make the Nov 1 payment, Ibarra said.

Tampa acted as a conduit for the original $84 million revenue bond issue that financed construction of the aquarium, but had no debt service obligation. That issue was backed by a $10 million letter of credit by the Port of Tampa, which owns the land where the aquarium sits.
As part of the refinancing agreement, the Port Authority will give the city $1.7 million and the land, valued at $8.3 million. In exchange the city will release the port from its letter of credit.

The aquarium is a nonprofit entity and will continue to be run by its 34-member board, iwth John Racanelli as president. However the city council approved a resolution giving it the option of revisiting the management structure within 90 days.
The refinancing is expected to reduce debt service costs by $20 million to $40 million,
